lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It snowed all night. One set of footprints. They only went in.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Old Tom, the gardener at Larkfield Manor, was in the shed. He would not come out again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Rosa, the cook, found him at ten. Hers were the only footprints in the snow.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: Nobody else came near that door. Nobody could have. The snow tells us so.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: The snow tells us what it saw. That is not the same as what happened.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: Kiri, you always say that. Fine. Who are we looking at?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: First, Rosa, the cook. She cooked dinner for the house from five o'clock.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: I went to the shed at ten to bring Tom his soup. I opened the door. That is all.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Two kitchen girls say she never left the stove before eight.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: So she walked to the door, and her prints go in. Simple.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Next, Mr. Hale, a guest. He sat at the family table from eight until eleven.

lines.speaker: Mr. Hale
lines.text: Dinner, then cards. Ask anyone. I never went near the garden.

lines.speaker: Mr. Hale
lines.text: I did hear Tom singing in his shed at eight, from the terrace. He was alive and in good voice.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: So whatever happened was after eight. And after eight, the snow was falling.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Last, Ben, the groundsman's son. He lives at the cottage by the gate.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I came home from the village at ten, through the snow. I went straight to bed.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: Three alibis, one dead end. Kiri, I do not see how this is possible.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Now watch closely. Three clues are hiding in plain view. Can you find them before Kiri does?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Clue one. The shed step. Look at the snow around it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: On the step there is a dark, dry outline. Snow is everywhere, except in that shape.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Snow cannot fall where something already lies. He was on that step when the snow began.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Clue two. The lantern by the door.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: Tom lit it every evening at dusk. Half past six, like clockwork.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Tonight it is cold, and the oil is full. It was never lit.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: So Tom was gone before half past six. He never sang at eight.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Clue three. Ben's boots.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He says he walked through deep snow at ten. His boots are dry, and warm from the fire.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: All right. I was home before eight, before it snowed. I was afraid you would blame me.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: On my way past the garden at half past six I saw Mr. Hale come out of the shed alone.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: So here is how it worked. Step one. Tom died before half past six, on that step.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Step two. At eight the snow began and covered every track of the one who was there.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Step three. Mr. Hale told us he heard singing at eight, so everyone thought it happened later.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Step four. At ten Rosa found him and made the only footprints left. The snow did the rest.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: Mr. Hale, there was no light in that shed at eight. The lantern was cold.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: He needed us to believe the snow made it impossible. It only made it quiet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The motive is two lines long. Tom had seen Mr. Hale burying a small box in the garden.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Mr. Hale did not want anyone to ask what was in it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The three clues were there the whole time. A dry outline. A cold lantern. A pair of dry boots.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: What do you walk past every day without really looking?

scenes.title: One set of footprints
scenes.place: The garden shed at night under falling snow, one line of footprints in the snow leading to its shut door, an unlit lantern hanging beside it

scenes.title: Rosa
scenes.place: The warm manor kitchen at night, a big pot on the stove, a cook in an apron wiping her hands, a clock on the wall

scenes.title: Mr. Hale
scenes.place: The manor dining room at night, candles on a long table, a guest in a velvet jacket folding his napkin, snow at the window

scenes.title: Ben
scenes.place: The groundsman's cottage porch at night, snow falling, a young man stamping his boots by a lamp

scenes.title: The first clue
scenes.place: A close view of the shed step in the snow, a dry dark outline of a lying shape on the boards with snow all around it

scenes.title: The second clue
scenes.place: A close view of the lantern hanging by the shed door, its glass clear and its oil full, snow on its hook

scenes.title: The third clue
scenes.place: A close view of a young man's boots on the cottage porch, dry and clean, a puddle-free boards, a warm lamp glowing

scenes.title: The trick
scenes.place: The garden under snow in the dark, a drawing of a clock at six and a second clock at eight with snow falling, the shed and the manor lit in the distance

scenes.title: Why
scenes.place: The manor terrace at night, snow on the stone rail, lights from the dining room behind, Kiri looking out over the white garden
